correctness.rationale: The all-order exceptional set and three-component decomposition follow from two explicit hub-to-hub paths in each direction plus a constructive strongly connected residual class; complement and reversal cover the symmetries. A separate overlap argument proves diameter k after either constant deletion. Every table entry is exhaustive over \(2^k\) failed vertices and all ordered surviving pairs; an independent string-graph SCC/BFS program agrees through \(k=7\). Limits are explicitly \(2\le k\le10\) for the histogram.

evidence: Muñoz and Gómez (1998), §3 Corollary 1 gives Δ nearly disjoint short routes in B(Δ,D), not postdeletion diameter tables or the complete SCC decomposition for the binary \(\Delta=2\) case.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A dominating theorem must imply the same directed induced-subgraph all-fault distribution. Generic connectivity, fixed-route overlay diameter, and undirected fault-tolerant routing operate on different invariants, so their conclusions do not subsume the stated classification. An unavailable historical full text remains a separate explicit risk.

The 1988 full-text access limit is a genuine residual originality risk, not a fabricated negative comparison.

originality.rationale: The prior-implication comparison excludes classical κ=1 and baseline diameter k as new. The candidate contribution is the explicit classification of every exceptional failed vertex, precise SCC sizes, and full finite directed fault-diameter distributions. Inspected primary sources address baseline connectivity, nearly disjoint routes, modified networks, undirected routing or fixed-route overlays, not these finer precise statements. One plausible older full paper is not accessible, so a genuine residual bibliographic risk remains. No absence-of-search uniqueness claim is made.
residual_risks: Du and Hwang 1988 original complete text unavailable; connectivity proofs could contain an equivalent fine-grained decomposition.
Some historical directed-network routing tables or unpublished computations may already encode these finite histogram values.

value.rationale: Fault survivability and directed postfailure worst-pair latency are canonical interconnection-network reliability invariants. The infinite theorem locates *all* single nodes whose failure actually fragments the network and gives the exact size of every resulting strongly connected component, rather than merely a known one-vertex connectivity bound. The finite exact table stratifies every failure by achievable diameter through order ten, detects a sharp three-extra-hop worst-case at \(k=5\) and a nonmonotone overhead at \(k=6\); this is a motivated complete small-network robustness benchmark, not an arbitrary graph subset or sampled experiment.
